newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent crude firm, but physical still pressure.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent crude firm, but physical still pressure.

text.p: North Sea markets saw little action on Wednesday as traders awaited the remaining December loading programmes and watched with interest the fate of the end November Brent cargoes.
Dec Brent gained over half a dollar to trade at 1843 GMT at $23.51 a barrel.
The last three November loading Brent cargoes were deferred into early December by the equity holders on Wednesday.
Physical deals included two Brent cargoes -- a Nov 20-22 at Dec -48 cents for a minimum sized cargo and a Nov 26-28 at a dated Brent related price, thought around dated evens.
Although no ships were seen fixed by the major now holding five end-Nov Brent cargoes, some traders felt these cargoes had already been onsold.
In late talk intermonth spreads were around +28/32 cents for Dec/Jan, +43/47 for Jan/Feb and +46/50 for Feb/Mar.
An early Dec Statfjord cargo also traded, at a healthy dated Brent +15.

The CFD market gained some four cents in late trade with one or two main players seen. Some pointed to Thursday's expiry of the December Brent contract on the IPE futures as an explanation of the late gains.
"Tomorrow is going to be a very interesting day. We have the APIs, the December expiry and probably some more (North Sea) loading programmes," one trader said.

In the Mediterranean, at least two large and two small Urals cargoes were still available for November, while prompt demand was relaxed. Differentials were talked lower at Dated Brent -75/-85 cents as a result.

Given a lack of buying interest until the last decade November, sellers said they were not overly concerned about weather-related and bureaucratic delays at Novorossiisk which threatened to push some loadings back to early December.
"The second decade of November is more or less covered," a trader said. "But there should be some demand in the third decade from Lavera."
A prompt 80,000-tonne cargo was sold at Dated Brent -70 cents delivered into Israel on Tuesday, the equivalent of cif Augusta values of -66/67 cents, dealers said.

But most traders said the deal was above market levels because of its prompt nature and exceptionally strong demand into Israel with Urals still offering refiners betters netbacks than other sour grades, including Egyptian.
Another two 130,000-tonne vessels could be heading for Israel soon, said one trader.
Traders said negotiations for Syrian December term contract prices were set to start on Thursday. Some expected a sharp reduction in differentials.
"The Syrian netback values are so low that Syrian Light should be brought down to around (Dated Brent) -30," a trader said.
In November Syrian Light term contract prices were set at Dated Brent -5 cents.
On Wednesday Nigeria reduced its official term crude prices to 15-23 cents for December exports.
December prices were down 18 cents for Bonny Light and Qua Iboe at Dated +45 cents. The prices could prove problematic for term lifters due to narrow profit windows, some traders said.
"Bonny-Qua Iboe is at best plus 45 cents on the market. Term lifters might have a lot of problems this month," said one.
-- Siobhan Hayden, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8978
